title: New Seka Spear review: Better than a Specialized Tarmac SL8?

takeaways.text: The 'wind eye' openings at the seatstay junction are the signature feature; the one-piece bar has a flat, broad top profile he finds uncomfortable when climbing.
Frame and fork retail at £2,250 in the UK, half a Tarmac SL8 frameset; frame weight is closer to a non-S-Works SL8, and SEKA offers a lifetime warranty but no complete bikes.
Fast but not electric; on his test loop it was slower than pure aero bikes but quicker than a Van Rysel RCR, and it reminds him of a Tarmac SL7.
The front end is very stiff and harsh on rough roads while seated comfort is excellent, so the bike feels unbalanced front to rear.
Five standard sizes plus two race sizes with lower stack and longer reach; at 181 cm he chose L with a 110 mm stem and no spacers.

disclosure: Sponsored segment for an unrelated camera; how the frame was obtained is not stated. The frame is a standard Spear judging by his £2,250 frameset price and weight comparison, built with Ultegra Di2 rather than the candidate's 105 Di2.
summary: A first-month ride review of the SEKA Spear built with Ultegra Di2, compared with the Specialized Tarmac SL8.
